Adding small perturbations to an image can cause a big change in model performance. To test security vulnerabilities of ML models an important tool is adversarial machine learning. The Fast Gradient Sign Attack (FGSM) is a type of adversarial attack. It's a white box attack (i.e. the attacker knows the model, the parameters and the architecture). It is designed to attack neural networks using gradients. The attack uses the gradient of the loss w.r.t the input data, then adjusts (perturb) the input data to maximize the loss. ## Projected Gradient Descent Attack Implementation. PGD is a variant of FGSM applied iteratively with projection. It is a commonly used attack for adversarial training: training the network to be robust. results.title: On the Definition of Robustness and Resilience of AI Agents for Real-time Congestion Management | AI Research Paper Details
results.content: This research introduces a novel methodology for quantitatively assessing the robustness and resilience of AI agents designed for real-time congestion management in electrical grids, directly addressing requirements in the EU AI Act while providing concrete testing procedures. Robustness metrics quantify an AI system's ability to maintain performance under perturbations. *Comparison of robustness metrics across different perturbation agents, showing how performance degrades under various attack scenarios.*. The methodology provides quantitative metrics that enable systematic assessment of AI agents under various perturbation scenarios, addressing a critical requirement of the EU AI Act. The case study reveals that RL-based agents show varying susceptibility to different types of perturbations, with intelligent adversarial agents revealing significant vulnerabilities compared to random or gradient-based approaches. By providing concrete implementation of robustness and resilience assessment, this work contributes to the development of AI systems that can not only perform well under ideal conditions but maintain acceptable performance and recover quickly when faced with disruptions - essential qualities for AI deployment in high-risk domains like power grid management.

results.title: (PDF) Are Time-Series Foundation Models Deployment-Ready? A Systematic Study of Adversarial Robustness Across Domains
results.content: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs), which are pretrained on large-scale, cross-domain data and capable of zero-shot forecasting in new scenarios without further training, are increasingly adopted in real-world applications. However, as the zero-shot forecasting paradigm gets popular, a critical yet overlooked question emerges: Are TSFMs robust to adversarial input perturbations? To address this gap, we conduct a systematic investigation into the adversarial robustness of TSFMs. Our results show that even minimal perturbations can induce significant and controllable changes in forecast behaviors, including trend reversal, temporal drift, and amplitude shift, posing serious risks to TSFM-based services.
